content: The lame man rides a horse, the handless drives a herd, the deaf man fights and does well; better to be blind than burned on a funeral pyre—a dead man is of use to no one.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Haltr ríðr hrossi (Hávamál, Stanza 71) — Poetic Edda
explanation: This verse presents an uncompromising rejection of victimhood and self-pity. Life may shatter your limbs, take your hearing, or dim your eyes, yet as long as breath remains in your lungs, you have the capacity to contribute, fight, and adapt. Despair is an early funeral; life belongs to those who keep moving forward.
practicalInsight: Stop lamenting what you lack or have lost. Focus your full energy today on what you can still do with the strength you have.
reflectionPrompt: What limitation or wound have you used as an excuse to sit on the sidelines of your life?
